liner.body_md:
## What listeners single out

- **Sugaree** (2 reviews): An eleven-minute performance contained lyrical mistakes typical of that year; Sugaree was the roughest performance, sounding rough despite occasional ramp-ups [11][18]
- **Visions of Johanna** (2 reviews): Visions of Johanna was described as beautiful and poignant by the reviewer; Visions of Johanna was the only impressive part of the otherwise bad show [18][20]
- **Jack Straw** (1 review): A strong opening performance of Jack Straw set the tone for the show [13]
- **China Cat Sunflower** (1 review): The China Cat Sunflower to I Know You Rider transition was the weakest all year [12]

## The recordings

- **gd1995-07-08.sbd.larson.35157.flac16** (recommended): soundboard; 20 songs; 151 min; rated 3.2/5 by 10 [1]
- **gd1995-07-08.sbd.miller.114363.flac16**: soundboard; 19 songs; 156 min; rated 2.86/5 by 14 [3]
- **gd95-07-08.BK401s.4362.sbeok.shnf**: audience recording; 19 songs; 160 min; rated 3.6/5 by 20 [5]. Said about its sound: Audience recording has little crowd noise, diffuse sound, but natural transparency [14]
- **gd95-07-08.sbd.10071.sbeok.shnf**: matrix (soundboard mixed with audience mics); 19 songs; 150 min; rated 2.68/5 by 44 [7]. Said about its sound: Sound quality was rated great, though the band's performance was average; Sound quality was very good, with Eternity patched from an audience recording [11][13]
- **gd1995-07-08.sbd.larson.tetzeli.fix-35157.98576.flac16**: soundboard; 17 songs; 144 min; rated 4.25/5 by 4 [10]

## Around the show

- Weather in Chicago was described as just about perfect for the concert [11]
- Crowd energy shines through strongly during the Visions of Johanna performance [14]
- Listener anticipated one more night of Vince's hurdy-gurdy before being free [17]
- Reviewer was sixteen years old attending their only Grateful Dead show [19]
- Quiet atmosphere with people twirling, though litterbugs and misbehavers were present [22]
- The Band opened the show, and Weir played acoustic on Eternity [3]
- Attendee left with a smile, a second-degree sunburn, and a joyful attitude [25]
- Jerry Garcia attended both of the final two Grateful Dead shows in Chicago [28]
- Described as the worst show attended with Jerry, featuring lyric flubs everywhere [12]
- Audience version of Visions of Johanna preferred for crowd energy over SBD [15]
- Show was not as bad as others in 1995, but still disappointing [20]

## Tapers and lineage

- **gd1995-07-08.sbd.larson.35157.flac16**: transferred by Chris Larson; source: S > ? > C [1]
- **gd1995-07-08.sbd.miller.114363.flac16**: transferred by Charlie Miller; source: SBD -> Dat (44.1k) [3]. Also: This is the only purely digital source in circulation for the date [3]
- **gd95-07-08.BK401s.4362.sbeok.shnf**: taped by Marc Nutter; transferred by Bill Gardner; source: Audience: B&K 4006's [5]
- **gd95-07-08.sbd.10071.sbeok.shnf**: transferred by Paul B; source: Soundboard patched with Audience [7]
- **gd1995-07-08.sbd.larson.tetzeli.fix-35157.98576.flac16**: source: Pitch-adjusted version of shnid 35157 [10]. Also: Set II tracks were pitch-stretched using Mark Nutter's digital FOB as reference; Redundant tracks were discarded, and SBEs were fixed in pitch-corrected files [10]

## Art and photos

- Poster by Grateful Dead: [Grateful Dead Soldier Field - July 9, 1995](https://www.dead.net/show/july-9-1995) [24]
- Poster by Grateful Dead: [Grateful Dead Soldier Field - July 9, 1995](https://www.dead.net/show/july-9-1995) [30]
